metadata.title: Apple On Track To Become November’s Mag7 Winner — Nvidia Takes The Biggest Hit

content.text:
-
Apple's market capitalization is now nearly $2 trillion more than Microsoft's (MSFT), the second most valuable company in the U.S. stock market.
-
After sharp gains in recent months, Apple is now the least favorable among the Magnificent Seven group based on stock fundamentals and analyst projections.
-
Apple is developing its own autonomous AI agent to take on offerings from Meta and OpenAI.
Apple Inc. (AAPL) is emerging as an unexpected winner in a volatile month where investor attention and trading activity largely centered on the Anthropic (ANT) IPO and the unprecedented developments at Nvidia (NVDA).
Apple shares have gained over 3.3% so far in November, putting them on track for a fifth consecutive month of gains and widening the iPhone-maker's valuation gap with other Big Tech peers. AAPL was the best-performing Magnificent Seven stock.
Apple's market capitalization is now nearly $2 trillion more than Microsoft's (MSFT), the second most valuable company in the U.S. stock market. Nvidia, the worst Mag7 performer this month, dipped to the third spot with a $3.6 trillion market capitalization.
November was a rather volatile month. Anthropic delivered the biggest IPO in history, and its shares climbed 17% on the first day of trading, signaling strong sentiment for the AI trade that had been pressured lately.
Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and his subsequent ouster and rehiring, triggered a bust and boom in AI-linked stocks.
Nvidia is a key financier and partner for dozens of tech companies, making it central to the health of the broader tech market. Still, tech stocks fell again during Thanksgiving week, suggesting that concerns about AI's durability still linger.
In this challenging period, Apple holding steady has not gone unnoticed. The company, which has been in the spotlight for a series of new launches under CEO John Ternus, has deliberately kept its AI spending well below that of Big Tech peers, making its stock less vulnerable to swings in AI sentiment.
Apple has also received a largely positive response to its company-first iPhone Duo foldable phone, touchscreen MacBook Pro and HomeView smart home device, with fans looking ahead to a major product lineup in 2027 to mark the iPhone's 20th anniversary.
Apple Catalysts
Bloomberg reported on Nov. 19 that Apple is developing its own autonomous AI agent. It followed a previous report saying that Ternus was pushing software chief Craig Federighi to accelerate Apple's AI roadmap and make Siri more agent-like, potentially as early as next year.
